label: Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD Mesh Router (AFi-R)
description: AmpliFi HD Mesh Router: 1x 1G WAN + 4x 1G LAN, 802.11ac 3x3 (450 Mbps 2.4 GHz + 1300 Mbps 5 GHz), touchscreen, mesh controller.
notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti's AmpliFi datasheet: **Wi-Fi/Gigabit Ethernet, (1) WAN, (4) LAN**, 802.11ac **13 Mbps to 1300 Mbps** (MCS0-MCS9, VHT 20/40/80) on 5 GHz and 802.11n **6.5 to 450 Mbps** on 2.4 GHz, with a touchscreen on the front. **Five copper ports, no PoE anywhere** - the router is a mesh controller first and a switch second. The **AFi-HD kit is this router plus two AFi-P-HD MeshPoints**, and the NVIDIA Gamer's Edition is this hardware in another shell; the MeshPoint's own port count is not stated in this datasheet, which is why it has no entry of its own yet.

label: Ubiquiti PowerBeam 5AC Gen2 (PBE-5AC-Gen2)
description: airMAX PowerBeam 5AC Gen2 5 GHz CPE/bridge: 1x 1G Ethernet port, passive 24 V PoE in, 802.11ac 2x2, 25 dBi dish.
notes: Vendor figures from the PowerBeam AC Gen2 datasheet: **(1) 10/100/1000 Ethernet port**, **passive PoE on pairs 4,5+/7,8-**, 24 V 0.5 A Gigabit PoE adapter included, 20-26 VDC input. **One port and it is gigabit** - the M-series PowerBeams next to it are fast ethernet, so a Gen2 mixed into an M-only estate is the one that can actually use a gigabit backhaul. The PoE is **passive 24 V, not 802.3af/at**: a standard PoE switch will not power it, and the included adapter is what does.
